run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: Investigated the signup failure in namespace app-162 (the signup-service and payments-service workloads live there; neither exists in otel-demo). Both signup-service pods (signup-service-7c89545dc9-j4s8v and signup-service-7c89545dc9-k2xvj) are Running with container Ready=false (ContainersNotReady) and appear in the signup-service Endpoints only as notReadyAddresses, so the signup Service has no ready backends. Their own logs show repeated '/ready 503' with 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>'. The dependency, payments-service, is the failing link: its single pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-8std8 logs 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' and 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', answers /health and /ready with 503, produced two Warning 'Unhealthy' events (Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503) at 07:19:45 and 07:19:55, and its Endpoints list only notReadyAddresses, which is consistent with the connection-refused error signup sees. The payments-service Deployment reads STRIPE_API_KEY from Secret payments-secrets key stripe-api-key and DATABASE_URL from the same Secret (key database-url); signup's PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL is set to http://payments-service:8080 as expected. No NetworkPolicies and no ResourceQuotas exist in the cluster, so policy/quota blocking is not the cause, and the payments container has 0 restarts with no terminated state, so crash/OOM is not the cause. Runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook was fetched and its steps were worked: pod status/logs and events (step 1), payments pods/logs (step 2), service-to-service reachability via Pod Ready/Endpoints instead of kubectl exec (step 3, no exec tool), Stripe and database greps in the payments log (step 4: Stripe error found, no database error lines), and env wiring from the Deployment specs (step 5: references readable, Secret values not readable). Metrics/traces sources were unavailable, so no error-rate, latency or trace corroboration exists for this Run. Because the invalid STRIPE_API_KEY value itself was only observed through the service's own error log (Secrets cannot be read), the conclusion is supported but the exact Secret content and when it was set remain unverified.

claims.text: signup-service in namespace app-162 runs 2 pods (signup-service-7c89545dc9-j4s8v, signup-service-7c89545dc9-k2xvj), both phase Running with container Ready=false and pod condition Ready=False reason ContainersNotReady, restartCount 0.

The signup-service Endpoints object in app-162 contains only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.32 j4s8v, 10.244.0.33 k2xvj), i.e. no ready backend for the signup-service Service (ClusterIP 10.96.8.221, port 8080).

Both signup-service pods log 'ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1 503' at 07:19:41, 07:19:46 and 07:19:51 on 2026-11-25.

payments-service pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-8std8 logs at startup 'ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', then 'ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' with 'GET /health HTTP/1.1 503' and repeated 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1 503'.

payments-service pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-8std8 has container Ready=false and pod Ready=False reason ContainersNotReady, with 0 restarts and no last termination state, and produced a Warning event 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503' at 07:19:45 and 07:19:55.

The payments-service Endpoints object in app-162 lists only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.34, pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-8std8) on port 8080, so requests to the payments-service ClusterIP 10.96.42.237:8080 have no ready backend.

Deployment payments-service (app-162, revision 1, replicas 1) sets env STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef payments-secrets/stripe-api-key, DATABASE_URL from payments-secrets/database-url and PORT=8080, with liveness /health and readiness /ready on port 8080; its Available condition is False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable and availableReplicas/readyReplicas are unset.

Deployment signup-service (app-162, revision 1, replicas 2) sets env PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080, DATABASE_URL from secretKeyRef signup-secrets/database-url and PORT=8080; its Available condition is False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable and availableReplicas/readyReplicas are unset.

Only one ReplicaSet exists per workload (payments-service-6d94c44fdc, signup-service-7c89545dc9), both created 2026-11-25T07:19:35Z, and the pods started at 2026-11-25T07:19:35Z, so the workloads were freshly created rather than rolled out from an earlier revision.

Cluster-wide there are 0 NetworkPolicy objects (query returned an empty list with status ok, total_items_processed 0) and 0 ResourceQuota objects, so neither inter-pod network policy nor quota exhaustion explains the connection refused between signup and payments.

payments-service crash-looping, being OOMKilled or evicted is rejected: its pod is Running with restartCount 0, lastState.terminated is null, no OOMKilled/Evicted signal appears in the pod data, and the app-162 events show only Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started plus Unhealthy liveness-probe failures.

A pod-lifecycle/startup artefact alone does not explain the failure: the probes had long since passed their initialDelaySeconds (payments liveness 2s, readiness 2s; signup readiness 5s) and the payments log states the failure cause is an invalid STRIPE_API_KEY, not slow startup.

Root cause hypothesis: the value of Secret payments-secrets key stripe-api-key (namespace app-162), injected into payments-service as STRIPE_API_KEY, is an invalid Stripe key; that makes the payments service answer 503 on /health and /ready, keeps its Endpoints in notReadyAddresses so callers get connection refused, and thereby blocks signup-service readiness and user registration.

Verify and correct Secret payments-secrets key stripe-api-key in namespace app-162 with a valid Stripe key (Secrets were not readable in this Run, so its current content was not inspected directly), then let the payments-service pod re-read it (for example recreate/restart Deployment payments-service) and confirm GET /health and GET /ready return 2xx before checking that payments-service Endpoints gains ready addresses.

Re-check signup-service after payments recovers: expect 'Payments service check failed ... Connection refused' in signup logs to stop, /ready to return 200, and both signup pods to appear as ready addresses in the signup-service Endpoints.

Because the failure is Stripe-API-key related, follow the standing escalation note and route it to the interlock team (other, non-Stripe issues go to the capricorn team); this is a process instruction, not evidence.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for this Run: get_label_values on traces_span_metrics_calls_total, execute_prometheus_instant_query('up') and get_label_values returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Therefore no error-rate, request-rate, latency or ERROR series for signup-service or payments-service could be read, and missing series are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable for this Run: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level evidence (status codes, error spans, call edges) for signup or payments exists; signup and payments are also absent from the traces tool's advertised service list, and neither name was confirmed in any trace data.

Secret payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key, key database-url) and Secret signup-secrets (key database-url) could not be read, and the code mounted from the 'app-code' Secret volume could not be read; the invalid-key conclusion rests on the payments-service's own log line, not on the Secret content. The exact key value and the time it was set are unknown.
No change_history integration is available, so when or by whom the STRIPE_API_KEY value was changed cannot be determined.

A cluster-wide ConfigMap query for names or data matching 'signup|payments|stripe|Stripe|STRIPE' returned status no_data (0 of 21 ConfigMaps matched), so no fault-injection ConfigMap was identified for these workloads; this is an empty query result, not proof that no such setting exists elsewhere (for example in the otel-demo flagd configuration).

kubectl exec / in-pod env inspection and port-forward connectivity tests from runbook step 3 and 5 were not possible with the available tools; reachability was assessed only from Pod Ready conditions, Endpoints subsets and application logs.

All app-162 objects and events appear from 2026-11-25T07:19:35Z onwards (RBAC and audit history of earlier state, and any earlier incident, are unavailable), so no pre-window baseline of signup or payments behaviour exists.

No user-facing signup request traffic (registrations) appears in the pod logs — only kubelet probe requests from 10.244.0.1 — so the claim that users cannot register rests on the reported symptom plus the fact that signup has no ready endpoints; end-user impact was not directly observed.
next_steps: Read or rotate Secret payments-secrets/stripe-api-key in app-162 with a valid Stripe key and confirm the payments-service /health and /ready endpoints then return 2xx.

After the key is fixed, verify payments-service Endpoints gains a ready address, then verify both signup-service pods become Ready and /ready returns 200 with no 'Payments service check failed' log lines.
Separately validate Secret signup-secrets/database-url, since signup's database dependency was not exercised by any observed request and its value is unreadable.
Once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable, confirm the correlated error-rate and span-status evidence for payments-service /health, /ready and signup registration requests.
Escalate to the interlock team per the standing instruction on Stripe/Stripe-API-related issues.
